recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If the checked-in medication SVG diagrams are still used by the build, regenerate or review them separately because they still mention the retired resource-level element; do not treat that as a FHIR-25051 semantic source fix while the authoritative definitions are correct.
issue_request: FHIR-25051 was Published/Persuasive for R5 by Pharmacy. It requested a way to convey an overall set of dosage instructions spanning multiple Dosage entries for MedicationRequest, MedicationDispense, and MedicationStatement/MedicationUsage, with renderedDosageInstruction identified as the then-current name to add.
initial_application: Jira comments record that renderedDosageInstruction was added to MedicationRequest, MedicationDispense, and MedicationUsage, and cite commit 80c2f73ea490c414129d8406d6d00d4e94af04c0. That commit added resource-level renderedDosageInstruction elements beside the Dosage-valued dosageInstruction/dosage elements.
additional_context: Current build-scope source has evolved: fhir.ini lists DosageDetails and active MedicationRequest, MedicationDispense, and MedicationStatement resources. The current StructureDefinitions type MedicationRequest.dosageInstruction, MedicationDispense.dosageInstruction, and MedicationStatement.dosage as 0..1 DosageDetails. DosageDetails.renderedInstruction is now 1..1 and defined as the full representation of the dosage instructions. R6 ballot notes on all three resources explicitly say renderedDosageInstruction was removed from the resources and placed in DosageDetails.renderedInstruction, and FHIR-54014 later made that rendered instruction required. Remaining old-name hits are compatibility mapping lines or generated-looking SVG diagrams, not the authoritative model.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Re-adding a resource-level renderedDosageInstruction would conflict with the current DosageDetails design, while the current required DosageDetails.renderedInstruction preserves FHIR-25051's semantic requirement for an overall dosage text.
